summary:
Olympus Health is a full-stack astronaut health exploration platform built around an interactive 3D human model. Users can select anatomical regions to access related health indicators, visualize historical measurements, review exploratory projections, receive rule-based alerts, and explore exercise plans.
One of the biggest advantages of our project is how simple and easy it is to use. Astronauts can easily navigate through the different features and understand their health data without needing advanced medical knowledge. Οur goal is to make health monitoring easier for astronauts, not more complicated.
details:
We built Olympus Health to make astronaut health data easier to understand. Our platform uses an interactive 3D human body to connect measurements with the anatomy they describe. Users can explore muscles, bones, and internal organs, select a region, and view related health indicators and historical charts.

The application combines health monitoring, exploratory 1-, 7-, 14-, and 30-day forecasts, and alerts that highlight measurements requiring attention. It also includes a seven-day exercise planner that balances resistance and aerobic training within available time and simplified fatigue constraints. This prediction is implemented using an MPC ( Model Predictive Control).

We used NASA’s Human Research Roadmap, the published bone-density model from Axpe et al., and bone-quality and biomarker findings from Gabel et al.’s TBone study. Limited access to individual astronaut records was a major challenge, so we generated clearly labeled synthetic demonstration data using Monte Carlo sampling. We kept published findings, simulated records, and calculated projections separate. Our forecasts and exercise plans demonstrate the concept and still require clinical validation.

We developed the project using JavaScript/JSX, Python, SQL, HTML, and CSS. Our main tools were React, Three.js, React Three Fiber, Drei, Vite, Node.js, Express, MySQL, FastAPI, NumPy, and SciPy. We adapted anatomy models from an open source Github repository. Also used Postman for testing our APIs.

Our creative approach makes the body itself the navigation system, bringing anatomy, health trends, and exercise planning into one experience. Throughout development, we considered usability, scientific accuracy, data limitations, and realistic mission constraints. We want to help astronauts, researchers, and students explore complex health information more clearly, while building a foundation for future integration with validated measurements and wearable sensors.
